title: The Macro Architecture: CNS, PNS, & Somatic vs. Autonomic Networks
description: Differentiate the Central and Peripheral Nervous Systems, somatic voluntary pathways, and sympathetic vs. parasympathetic divisions.

slides.title: The Two Grand Divisions: CNS & PNS 🗺️
slides.content:
# The Macro Architecture of the Nervous System

The nervous system is divided into two primary anatomical domains:

1. **Central Nervous System (CNS)**: Composed of the **brain** and **spinal cord**, encased safely within bone (cranium and vertebral column). The CNS is the central hub for integrating sensory information and commanding behavior.
2. **Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)**: Composed of all nerve fibers and ganglia outside the brain and spinal cord, linking the CNS to sensory organs, muscles, and viscera.

### Divisions of the Peripheral Nervous System:
* **Somatic Nervous System (SNS)**: Mediates voluntary motor output to skeletal muscles and relays conscious somatic sensations (touch, pain, proprioception).
* **Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)**: Regulates involuntary visceral functions—heart rate, respiration, digestion, and glandular secretion.

quizData.question: Which of the following structures is exclusively part of the Central Nervous System (CNS)?
quizData.explanation: The CNS is composed strictly of the brain and spinal cord; peripheral nerves and ganglia belong to the PNS.

slides.title: The Autonomic Tug-of-War: Sympathetic vs. Parasympathetic ⚡
slides.content:
## Fight-or-Flight vs. Rest-and-Digest

The Autonomic Nervous System is divided into two physiologically opposing branches that maintain homeostatic balance:

| Feature | Sympathetic Nervous System (SNS) | Parasympathetic Nervous System (PNS) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Colloquial Nickname** | 'Fight or Flight' (Crisis/Arousal) | 'Rest and Digest' (Energy Conservation) |
| **Anatomical Origin** | Thoracolumbar spinal cord ($T_1 - L_2$) | Craniosacral (Cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X + Sacral $S_2 - S_4$) |
| **Ganglia Location** | Close to spinal cord (Sympathetic chain) | Close to or within target organs |
| **Pupils** | Dilate (Mydriasis for distance vision) | Constrict (Miosis) |
| **Heart Rate & Blood Flow** | Accelerates; shunts blood to skeletal muscles | Slows; directs blood to gut and kidneys |
| **Digestion & Salivation** | Inhibited; dry mouth, slowed motility | Stimulated; abundant watery saliva, active peristalsis |
| **Postganglionic Neurotransmitter** | **Norepinephrine** (mostly) | **Acetylcholine (ACh)** |

quizData.question: When you encounter an immediate threat, which autonomic response occurs?

options.text: Sympathetic activation: pupil dilation, bronchodilation, and elevated heart rate
Parasympathetic release of acetylcholine onto cardiac pacemaker cells

quizData.explanation: Sympathetic activation triggers the fight-or-flight response: pupils dilate, airways widen (bronchodilation), and heart rate spikes to prepare muscles for action.

slides.title: Neuroscience Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
### The Enteric Nervous System: The Second Brain

Did you know your gastrointestinal tract contains over **500 million neurons**? Termed the **Enteric Nervous System**, this autonomous network embedded in the gut wall can coordinate digestion, gut motility, and hormone secretion even if completely severed from the brain!
